title: Senior's toolkit: errors, files and logs
summary: logging set up properly, exception chaining, pathlib, json options and dev mode: the tools for Python that fails well.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: errors, files and logs
steps.body: Robust code tells you what went wrong: a log line with a traceback, a chained exception with the real cause, a path that works from any folder. These are the calls experienced Python developers use for it.

toolkit.what: Configure logging once, at the program's entry point. Each module then uses `logging.getLogger(__name__)`, never `print`.
flags: the lowest level that is shown
time, level and which module logged it
replace handlers someone else already set up

toolkit.what: Inside an `except` block: logs at ERROR level with the full traceback. Pass values as arguments, not by building the string yourself.
flags: the string is only built if the level is enabled

toolkit.what: Raise your own exception while keeping the original as its cause. The traceback shows both, joined by "The above exception was the direct cause".
flags: hide the original when it is only noise
toolkit.example:
except json.JSONDecodeError as err:
    raise SettingsError(f"{path} is not valid JSON") from err

toolkit.what: Paths as objects: join with `/`, read and write in one call, find files with glob.
flags: always say the encoding; the default differs per OS
create the folder and its parents; no error if it exists
the folder of this source file, not the current directory

toolkit.what: Turn data into JSON. The options decide whether dates and decimals work and whether output is diff-friendly.
flags: fall back to `str()` for types JSON does not know (dates, Decimal)
stable key order, so files diff cleanly
keep non-ASCII text as-is instead of `\u` escapes

toolkit.what: Ignore one specific, expected exception, readably. Never use it (or a bare `except:`) for errors you have not thought about.
flags: "it is fine if the file is already gone"

toolkit.what: Development mode: shows warnings Python normally hides, like a file you never closed (ResourceWarning) or a deprecated call.
flags: turn warnings into exceptions, so tests fail on them

steps.prompt: The app crashes on start with this. What are the two problems?
code: During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "JSONDecodeError") to str
options: `settings.json` is empty or not JSON (the root cause), and the `except` handler itself crashes; log with `log.exception("bad settings in %s", path)` instead
Only the `TypeError` matters: it is the last line
Line 4 of app.py is wrong because `Path` needs a full path
steps.explain: "During handling of the above exception" means the handler failed while dealing with the first error. Read both: the first block is why it failed (char 0 means the file is empty or starts with something that is not JSON), the second is a bug in your error handling.

JSON has no date or Decimal type, so plain `dumps` raises TypeError. `default=str` converts anything unknown with `str()`. `sort_keys=True` sorts the keys, which keeps files stable in version control.

steps.prompt: Set up logging once, get this module's logger, and log a failure with its traceback.
steps.explain: `getLogger(__name__)` names the logger after the module, so you can see and filter where a line came from. `log.exception` adds the traceback; `log.error` would log only the message.

steps.prompt: `python report.py` works from the project folder. The same script run by the scheduler fails with `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'templates/report.html'`. What is the robust fix?
options: Build the path from the script's location: `Path(__file__).parent / "templates" / "report.html"`
Tell the scheduler to always start in the project folder
Copy the templates folder to every directory
steps.explain: Relative paths are relative to the current working directory, which is wherever the process was started. `Path(__file__).parent` is fixed. Suppressing the error would just produce an empty report.

steps.prompt: Match each tool to the job.
pairs: wrap an error and keep its root cause
hide an internal error that is only noise
ignore one expected error on purpose
make sure an output folder exists
see hidden warnings such as unclosed files

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Configure logging once at the entry point and use `log.exception` in every handler that swallows or re-raises. When you catch and re-raise, chain with `from err` so the root cause survives, and run your tests with `-X dev` now and then to catch the warnings that become tomorrow's bugs.
